open_points.subject: external AI provider boundary
open_points.text: The Agent is “any language-model agent” running in VM Agent, while R0-68 refers to “the agent's AI provider” and the exclusions refer to “external AI providers”, but no actor or boundary says whether model requests leave VM Agent, who receives them, or which agent-visible values cross that boundary.
open_points.question: Does the agent call an external model provider, and if so, which Registry-derived values may be sent to it and under whose trust and retention rules?
options: The external provider receives every value exposed to the agent, but never Registry-classified `personal_data`
The model runs locally and no Registry-derived value crosses to an external provider
Only a specified subset of agent-visible fields may cross to named providers
open_points.default_guess: Treat the external model provider as outside the platform trust boundary and permit it to receive all agent-visible, non-`personal_data` outputs under the platform governance.

open_points.subject: customer erasure after fiscal data was added
open_points.text: “erase a customer's contact data” says the Customer “keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased” but enumerates only “name, phone, e-mail and language” as gone, after R0-80 added kind, tax id and legal name to the Customer record.
open_points.question: When this action succeeds, are kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state and relationship-end date also erased, or does some of that data survive?
options: Keep only `customer_ref` and the erased fact; remove every other customer field
Erase contact and fiscal values but retain non-personal state such as kind, restriction and relationship-end date
Erase only name, phone, e-mail and language; retain fiscal data and the other state
open_points.default_guess: Apply “keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased” literally and remove every other customer field.

open_points.subject: revision preconditions and revision visibility
open_points.text: R0-35 says “A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change moves. A change states the revision it was made against”, but the action table gives stale-revision failure only for project and customer correction, omits it for archive, customer erasure, restriction, relationship ending/resumption and project erasure, and `read a customer` does not return the revision needed to make those changes.
open_points.question: Which state-changing actions must receive an expected revision, which record revision does each move, and through which read output does the owner obtain the current customer revision?
options: Every action changing a Project or Customer requires its current revision, refuses a stale one and returns the next revision
Only correction actions use revisions; the other actions are unconditional
Some named actions use revisions and the remaining actions have separately declared concurrency behavior
open_points.default_guess: Require the current Project or Customer revision for every action that changes that record, expose the customer revision in customer reads, and return the resulting revision after success.

open_points.subject: answering an access request with an invalid project choice
open_points.text: “answer an access request” says granting adds “the project the owner picks from the catalogue” and lists only “a request no longer pending” as failure, while “grant a project to an agent session” refuses an unknown or archived project.
open_points.question: If the owner answers a pending request by selecting an unknown, archived, anonymised or otherwise ungrantable project, is the answer refused, and does the pending request remain or get cleared?
options: Apply the grant action's checks atomically; on failure keep the request pending
Clear the request as a decline when the selected project cannot be granted
Allow the answer to grant project states that the direct grant action refuses
open_points.default_guess: Apply the normal grant checks atomically and leave the pending request unchanged when the chosen project cannot be granted.

open_points.subject: customer identity during migration
open_points.text: R0-50 says import “keeps every identity and link: project ids, `customer_ref`s, room and pointer ids and versions”, while the import action says “a v1 `customer_ref` that is not a Registry-minted id becomes a new Customer with a minted `customer_ref`”, moving the old value to tax id when applicable.
open_points.question: Must import preserve every legacy `customer_ref`, or must it replace non-Registry identities with newly minted references and rewrite project links through a recorded mapping?
options: Mint replacements only for non-Registry references and rewrite all imported links atomically
Reject any selected project whose customer reference is not already a valid Registry identity
open_points.default_guess: Mint a new `customer_ref` for each non-Registry legacy reference and atomically rewrite imported links, preserving the legacy value only as tax id when valid.

open_points.subject: renaming imported archived projects
open_points.text: R0-82 says “Projects imported under a person's name (R0-79) are renamed by the owner after the import”, but R0-12 and `correct a project` say an archived project cannot be corrected, and import does not say that selected projects must be active or may be renamed as part of import.
open_points.question: How is an imported archived project whose display name contains a person's name brought into compliance with R0-82?
options: Permit a one-time rename during the import mapping and confirmation
Permit this specific correction after import even though the project is archived
Reject such a project from import
Allow the personal display name to remain on an archived imported project
open_points.default_guess: Let the owner supply the compliant display name in the confirmed import mapping before the project is written to production.
